bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The Rs.30.81cr New India Assurance deal is not just a one-off — it’s a multi-year recurring revenue anchor that validates the PSU digitalization play; SOC is not a cost center but a recurring service engine with proven pipeline, not yet reflected in P&L
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Integrated capability spanning data centre, cloud, cybersecurity, managed infrastructure and now connectivity, allowing the technology estate to be consumed under a single SLA, a single operating framework and a single accountable partner ('One Unified Technology Experience')
- Diversified vertical mix with no single vertical accounting for more than 29 percent of revenue (FY26: mid-market and other industries 28.5%, BFSI 20.9%, ITeS 19.3%, government and public sector 18.0%, telecommunications 13.3%)
- Direct ownership of last-mile connectivity following the Red Hut acquisition and the Athena IT & Telecom / AIT Internet Services investments, which added SD-WAN as a service, telecom integration and Class A ISP capability — described as making Orient one of the few Indian providers with such ownership
- Established institutional and public-sector franchise, including managing critical AWS workloads for Digital India Corporation such as DigiLocker and UMANG
- Deep OEM partnership network across AWS, Dell, Fortinet, Nutanix, HPE, Tableau, CrowdStrike, ThoughtSpot, Check Red and Securonix
- GPU-as-a-service collaboration with AWS India under the IndiaAI mission, placing Orient inside national-scale AI infrastructure build-out
- More than 1,500 professionals with over 300 years of combined leadership experience; 1,602 permanent professionals as of March 31, 2026 across India and Singapore
- Long-standing enterprise relationships and domain experience across regulated, mission-critical sectors
- Governance depth: a Board of eight directors including four independent directors and two women, with Audit, Nomination and Remuneration, Stakeholders Relationship and CSR committees each chaired by an independent director
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Margin pressure from hardware-led engagements — Management's MD&A risk table states hardware-led engagements and cost escalation can compress margins; the mitigation focus is to increase service mix, improve project execution and pricing discipline. This is structural for an infrastructure integrator whose revenue is partly product supply, and the AR notes FY26 margins carried the cost of paying for delivery capacity ahead of demand.
- Working-capital intensity — Receivable cycles and project billing can constrain cash generation; mitigation is tight receivables governance, milestone billing and collections discipline. The SWOT also flags that infrastructure/hardware-linked revenues carry higher working-capital requirements, and trade receivables run on 60 to 120 day credit terms.
- Customer concentration — The financial risk management note discloses that during the year two customers individually contributed more than 10% of total revenue. Management states it remains focused on broadening its customer base and reducing revenue concentration risk over time. (Disclosed in the financial-risk note routed to the profile and risks bundles of the same annual report.)
- Technology obsolescence — Rapid changes in AI, cloud and cybersecurity can reduce the relevance of existing capabilities; mitigation is continuous skills development, OEM partnerships and portfolio refresh. The SWOT separately lists rapid technology obsolescence and changing OEM platforms as a threat.
- Supply-chain and geopolitical risk / import dependence — Import dependence can affect the availability and cost of hardware; mitigation is diversified sourcing, planning and customer-level delivery management. The SWOT adds imported hardware cost and currency volatility, and supply-chain constraints and lead-time uncertainty, as threats. Foreign currency exposure, primarily to the US Dollar, is stated to be primarily unhedged under the Company's risk management policy.
- Cybersecurity and data risk — Security incidents can result in operational, financial and reputational consequences; mitigation is security-by-design, monitoring, resilience and compliance controls. Because Orient itself operates managed security and customer infrastructure, a breach would carry client-facing as well as internal consequences.
- Government / PSU execution cycles — Long procurement and implementation cycles can affect revenue timing and working capital; mitigation is strong project governance and contract / milestone management. Government and public sector contributed 18 percent of FY26 revenue, so this timing risk is material to the mix.
- Talent availability and retention of specialised skills — Competition for specialised technology skills can increase cost and attrition risk; mitigation is upskilling, retention and targeted hiring. The industry section notes the shift from volume-based hiring towards specialised skills in AI, cloud, cybersecurity, data engineering and infrastructure, requiring continued investment in workforce capability.
- Scale disadvantage and domestic market concentration — The SWOT lists smaller scale than large listed IT infrastructure integrators and domestic market concentration as weaknesses, and larger integrators with greater scale and purchasing power, plus OEM pricing pressure and intense competition, as threats.

- Capability build-out is presented as a staged 25+ year progression: founded 1997 selling computers and telefax machines; 1999 OEM partnerships for Data Centre Solutions; 2006 Managed Services; 2013 Cloud Services; 2017 Digital Transformation (RPA, BI, mobile & web apps, facility management); 2023 ESG under Sustainability Services; 2024 listing plus Cybersecurity & Digital Forensics and Remote Infrastructure Management (RIM).
- Customer base is described as "marquee" and diversified, attributed to "our ability to tailor and customise our product and services to suit the requirements of our customers"; Q1 2026-2027 industry-wise revenue share is BFSI 24.92%, ITES 16.82%, Government & PSU 12.29%, Telecommunication 1.92% and Mid-market & Others 44.06% (the last defined as healthcare, manufacturing, infrastructure, real estate, logistics, education, e-commerce, conglomerates, energy and service industries).

business.body:
- [Order book] Order Book of Rs 375.43 crore as of 12th August 2026, billable during FY27.

- [Industry TAM, CRISIL] All market-size and CAGR figures come from a Company-commissioned CRISIL report titled 'Analysis of IT Services, Cloud Computing and Data Centre in India' dated July 2024; headline Indian IT industry ~$246 Billion, split as IT Services ~$129 Billion, ITeS ~$45 Billion, Software Products and ER&D ~$54 Billion, Hardware ~$18 Billion.
- [Fastest-growing addressed markets] Per the same CRISIL report, India's Data Centre industry is projected at a FY23-27P CAGR of 30-35% (Rs 84.5 Bn to Rs 240-280 Bn) and Public Cloud Services at 22-28% (Rs 550 Bn to Rs 1,250-1,450 Bn) — the two fastest-growing of the markets the Company addresses.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Services First, Annuity Forward — accelerate the shift from transactional product supply towards services and annuity revenue, accepting near-term margin cost; services revenue grew 33 percent in FY26 and now approaches half of total revenue, and the intent is to lift recurring and annuity streams to a majority of revenue and restore EBITDA margins as contracts season.
- Own Every Layer of the Stack — build direct ownership across infrastructure, cloud, connectivity and security so enterprises consolidating vendors get one accountable partner; the Red Hut acquisition and the Athena IT & Telecom / AIT Internet Services investments added SD-WAN as a service, telecom integration and Class A ISP capability.
- Deliver 'One Unified Technology Experience' — the technology estate consumed under a single service level agreement, a single operating framework and a single accountable partner.
- Security at the Core — scale managed detection and response, identity governance and digital forensics into a flagship practice, backed by the Turbe SDC's next-generation SOC and the Securonix agentic-AI SIEM alliance.
- Deep Verticals, Wide India — grow government, BFSI and mid-market franchises while keeping no single vertical dominant, and expand international revenue from Singapore and the UAE.
- People, Partners and Platforms — expand certified capacity in cloud, security and AI operations across the OEM partner network (AWS, Dell, Fortinet, Nutanix, HPE, Tableau, CrowdStrike, ThoughtSpot, Check Red, Securonix) and keep growing leaders from within.
- Verticalisation as a growth engine — build deeper industry knowledge so teams recognise recurring industry problems and move the conversation from what technology a customer needs to what an industry requires technology to achieve.
- Account deepening over customer count — extend engagements that start with infrastructure into cloud, security, managed services, connectivity, workplace, applications, analytics and automation, so Orient matters more to customers it already has.
- Position around AI-ready infrastructure — the GPU-as-a-service collaboration with AWS India under the IndiaAI mission places Orient inside national-scale AI infrastructure build-out.
- Inorganic capability building — use investments in subsidiaries and associates to broaden the Group's technology ecosystem.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Orient's FY26 expansion was footprint-, capability- and inorganic-led rather than manufacturing capacity-led. The Service Delivery Centre at Turbe (Navi Mumbai) was commissioned in December 2025, bringing next-generation network and security operations centres, integrated ITSM and ITAM tooling and automation-backed operations into one high-availability environment; combined security monitoring capacity across a dual-site architecture now exceeds 8,000 security devices, supported by the Securonix alliance which added agentic AI-powered unified defence SIEM to the managed security stack. In October 2025 the Board approved the acquisition of Red Hut Innovation Technology Private Limited (100%, wholly-owned subsidiary, effective November 1, 2025) and strategic 46% investments in Athena IT and Telecom Solutions Private Limited and AIT Internet Services Private Limited (both effective December 1, 2025) — a combined commitment of ₹7.71 crore completed in roughly thirty days, adding SD-WAN as a service, telecom integration and Class A ISP / last-mile connectivity capability and strengthening the South India (Bengaluru) footprint. Capability build-out also includes a GPU-as-a-service collaboration with AWS India under the IndiaAI mission, placing Orient inside national-scale AI infrastructure provisioning. On IPO-funded capex, the Company acquired an office premise at Navi Mumbai (fully utilised) and set up NOC and SOC equipment at that Navi Mumbai property (fully utilised), while the Device-as-a-Service equipment purchase programme remains partly unutilised: implementation was postponed to Fiscal 2027 to align with customer requirements and following changes in vendor, specifications and quantity, with the balance of the NOC/SOC allocation to be transferred to DaaS. Shareholders approved a special resolution by postal ballot on March 26, 2026 extending the IPO-proceeds utilisation timeline to March 31, 2027. Delivery reach spans technical resources at more than 250 locations across India plus branch offices in Pune, Delhi, Chennai, Bengaluru and Ahmedabad and a Singapore branch (opened January 28, 2016), with stated ambition to expand international revenue from Singapore and the UAE. Headcount stood at 1,602 permanent professionals as of March 31, 2026 across India and Singapore.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The outlook for FY2026-27 remains favourable for technology infrastructure and services providers that can combine infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity, managed services and automation.
- NASSCOM expects FY27 to be a more mature phase of AI adoption, with technology expenditure broadly range-bound at 5-7% while AI budgets progressively increase, shifting competitive focus from experimentation towards measurable business outcomes.
- Continued enterprise digitisation, increasing cloud adoption, rising data volumes, expansion of AI workloads, growing cybersecurity requirements and ongoing data-centre capacity additions are expected to sustain technology investment.
- Increasing preference for managed and subscription-based technology models creates opportunities to build recurring and annuity revenue through managed infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity and Device-as-a-Service offerings.
- Expansion of Global Capability Centres and digital public infrastructure is creating demand for scalable, secure and resilient technology environments.
- Domestic data-centre and cloud investment is supported by enterprise requirements on latency, data residency, resilience, business continuity and regulatory compliance.
- Management's stated demand catalysts visible in its own pipeline: hyperscaler and data-centre investment, global capability centre expansion, data localisation, government digital missions in e-governance and citizen services, and the enterprise rush to secure and modernise infrastructure ahead of AI adoption.
- Domestic market sizing behind the segments: public cloud services in India projected to grow at 22 to 28 percent annually, data centres at 30 to 35 percent, IT hardware equipment and leasing underpinning DaaS at 10 to 11 percent, and domestic IT services at 6.5 to 7.5 percent.
- Margin lever: management states margins carried the cost of paying for delivery capacity, integration and leadership ahead of the demand it exists to serve, and expects margins to recover as service contracts season.
- Government and public sector contributed 18 percent of FY26 revenue, a franchise management intends to deepen, alongside strengthening cloud and application capabilities to serve more of the transformation journey.
- Entered FY27 with orders in hand of approximately ₹400 crore, described as among the strongest opening positions the Company has reported, weighted towards multi-year engagements whose economics improve with tenure.
- Marquee FY26 wins cited: infrastructure modernisation of approximately ₹22 crore for a digital-first financial institution; workplace transformation of approximately ₹15 crore for a large industrial and energy enterprise on a subscription basis; an aviation engagement of approximately ₹8.5 crore to ₹9 crore for a globally recognised airline group; and an enterprise storage and data infrastructure engagement of approximately ₹26 crore for a large public sector institution.
- Multi-year managed services contracts and the DaaS win of ₹15 crore strengthened the annuity base during FY26.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

Competition for specialised technology skills can increase cost and attrition risk; mitigation is upskilling, retention and targeted hiring. The industry section notes the shift from volume-based hiring towards specialised skills in AI, cloud, cybersecurity, data engineering and infrastructure, requiring continued investment in workforce capability.
